This year’s North America World Championship Qualify features two special guests: Ted Lewis and Billy Bob Thompson! Ted Lewis voiced Bakura and Bandit Keith from the original animated Yu-Gi-Oh! series, Jack Atlas from Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D’s and Yu-Gi-Oh! ARC-V, and Chumley Huffington from Yu-Gi-Oh! GX. Billy Bob Thompson voiced Gong Strong, Leo Akaba, and Declan Akaba from Yu-Gi-Oh! ARC-V, as well as Vector from Yu-Gi-Oh! Zexal. Take a look at how these two voice actors are enhancing WCQ attendees’ experiences this weekend!

Ted Lewis and Billy Bob Thompson have been making tournament-related announcements throughout the weekend in-character as Jack Atlas and Gong Strong respectively. Duelists have enjoyed hearing them, and many crack a smile when they realize Jack Atlas and Gong Strong are giving them information about the tournament.
In addition, both voice actors are participating in autograph sessions throughout the weekend.
Duelists have been lining up all weekend to get cards and Game Mats signed by Ted Lewis and Billy Bob Thompson.
Duelists throughout the weekend have also been thrilled to converse with their favorite voice actors as they received their autographs.
Ted Lewis and Billy Bob Thompson also autographed special Token Cards to be distributed to the staff members who helped to make this weekend’s tournament possible!

Finally, Ted Lewis and Billy Bob Thompson will reprise their roles as Jack Atlas and Gong Strong respectively and engage in a Live Duel for the entertainment of this weekend’s attendees! You can watch the Live Duel on Twitch and YouTube right before the Top 16 begins, so don’t miss out!

Paulie Aronson is both a Remote Duel, and in-person YCS Champion, a feat few can match. He’s always at the cutting edge of competition, showcasing his Dueling and Deck-building skills whenever possible. After qualifying for the 2023 World Championship in Tokyo, Japan on August 5-6th against 31 of the toughest Duelists in North America, we discuss what it means to him, his plans for the rest of the weekend at the NAWCQ now that the pressure is off, and much more.

r.b: How does it feel to be qualified for the 2023 World Championship?

r: It feels great! I’m super excited!

r.b: Has it had a chance to set in yet?

r: Yeah, it’s pretty cool. I was always more focused on performing well in the NAWCQ Main Event rather than qualifying for the World Championship. However, now that I’m going, I realize how exciting of an opportunity it is.

r.b: How do you feel about the unique Forbidden & Limited List for the event?

r: I love practicing for events, so I’m extremely excited to get to do it in a unique format.

r.b: Which part are you looking forward to the most?

r: Getting to meet the top players from all over the world, especially from Japan! I’m also excited to be traveling outside of the Americas for the first time as well.

r.b: What’s it like playing in the Main Event now, with the pressure of the World Championship qualification behind you?

r: I love competing and being at events in general. I’m just as motivated to win the NAWCQ as I was before this, so nothing has changed.

r.b: Are your Deck choices from the Main Event and the World Qualifying Points Playoffs different? If so, why?

r: I’m playing Kashtira for both actually! They’re very different, however. I spent a lot of time studying the competition for the playoffs and tried to gauge the likelihood of their choices, then tailored my Deck to that. That’s one of the most unique parts of the World Qualifying Points Playoff, is that every player is well-known, and you can study up on the competition.

r.b: What is your biggest piece of advice for an aspiring competitor, who wants to hit the pinnacle of competition like the World Championship?

r: Practice as much as possible! Seriously, play as much as you can. Learn as much as you can from everyone and learn as many strategies as possible. Also, when you’re deciding on a Deck for an event, make sure you play whatever you’re most comfortable and experienced with, comfort is key.

r.b: Is there anything you’d like to say before you get ready to compete in the Main Event?

r: I would really like to thank all my friends who have practiced with me so much and helped me to prepare for the event. I’m really looking forward to the World Championship!

Fresh off his win from the most recent Remote Duel YCS two weeks ago,

has made Top Cut of multiple YCS events overall, and now has successfully qualified for the World Championship in Tokyo, Japan on August 5-6! After Dueling through a field of other top contenders, he was kind enough to sit down and discuss this monumental achievement and what it means to him.

r.b: How does it feel to be qualified for the 2023 World Championship?

r: It feels good! It’s somewhat surreal and hasn’t truly hit me yet. I’m just trying to stay focused for the Main Event.

r.b: How do you feel about the unique Forbidden & Limited List for the event?

r: It’s very interesting. I think it’s something I will enjoy immensely, and having a new format to perform well in will be exciting, since there will be so many lesser-known Decks to try, like my Exosister Deck, which can be solid picks.
It’s also different than previous year’s World Championships because there won’t be as much of an established “best Deck” since the restrictions on each Deck are so strong.

r.b: What are you looking forward to the most?

r: Honestly, I’m looking forward to practicing for the event with my group. We all have such different perspectives and ideas on how to approach the game that it will be an exciting experience.

r.b: What’s it like playing in the Main Event now, with the pressure of the World Championship qualification behind you?

r: I don’t think it has changed much. I’ve spent a lot of time getting mentally prepared and focusing on my gameplay, not just the results of tournaments.

r.b: Are your Decks from the Main Event and the World Qualifying Points Playoffs different? If so, why?

r: The Main Deck is the same, but the Side Deck is different. For the Worlds Qualifying Points Playoff, my Side Deck was more focused on a smaller number of expected matchups.

r.b: What’s your biggest piece of advice for an aspiring competitor, who wants to hit the pinnacle of competition like the World Championship?

r: Don’t be results oriented in your thinking, focus on getting better and playing well consistently, if you do that the results will improve. Basically, try to play well and good things will happen, all in time.

r.b: Is there anything you’d like to say before you get ready to compete in the Main Event?

r: I wanted to thank my playtesting group for being so helpful, and my friends for supporting me during this!

Last weekend, Europe chose their Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME World Championship representatives at the 2023 European World Championship Qualifier in Utrecht, Netherlands. Now, it’s North America’s turn to select its competitors!

Today, a select 32 Duelists will compete in a single-elimination tournament that will determine 2 of those competitors. Tomorrow and on Sunday, the remaining Duelists who were invited to compete in the North America World Championship Qualifier (NAWCQ) will battle it out for the honor of representing North America at this year’s World Championship in Tokyo, Japan. The Top 4 Duelists in this weekend’s competition will qualify to compete in the Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME World Championship, and will receive paid travel and accommodations to compete, in addition to other incredible prizes. Those 4 Duelists will join the 2 Duelists from today and make up a team of 6 Duelists to represent North America at this year’s most honorable tournament.

In order to compete in the NAWCQ this weekend, Duelists needed to earn an invitation by triumphing in a Regional Qualifier event or another event awarding an invitation to compete in the NAWCQ. While this is no easy feat for most Duelists, the 32 Duelists competing in today’s exclusive event managed to earn invitations over and over again. Here’s how qualification for today’s World Qualifying Points Playoff worked.

Players participating in events that award invitations to the NAWCQ can win World Qualifying Points for achieving a rank that awards an invitation. The better the competitor’s rank in the tournament, the more World Qualifying Points they receive. Players accumulated as many points as possible for the 2019-2022 Extended Season and then again in the 2022-2023 Season. The 16 Duelists with the most World Qualifying Points for the 2019-2022 Extended Season and the 16 Duelists with the most World Qualifying Points for the 2022-2023 Season are invited to participate in today’s exclusive single-elimination event. Check here for more information about World Qualifying Points.
Each of the 32 Duelists participating today will receive VIP Status with a 2-Round Bye for the NAWCQ starting on Saturday, as well as an

prize card – but the real prize that these 32 Duelists have their eyes on is the invitation, travel, and accommodations to the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG World Championship 2023! Only the top 2 Duelists today will be awarded the honor of competing in the World Championship. The rest of them will need to try again tomorrow as they compete in a tournament against the thousands of other Duelists who earned an invitation to the NAWCQ.
